title: I Let the Rideshare Comfort Cancellation Fee Follow the Driver Who Ghosted

parts.text: I stood at arrivals with a Comfort pin for a car that circled twice and then went offline. The app said I cancelled. I had not. I was forty-five, rolling a suitcase in a storm. The driver, username StarPath, had texted wait by baggage even though I was already there. I screenshotted the pin, the circling map, the cancellation, and the text. Support's bot offered a $3 credit. I used the in-app report for driver-initiated cancel and attached the map. At 9:51 the same StarPath accepted a new Comfort ping two cars away from me, then messaged are you the suitcase.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He is pinging me again after the app billed me for his ghost.

social.video_title: He circled, dropped, and billed me for cancelling — Part 1/2
social.description: Arrivals, storm, $3 bot. Then he came back for the suitcase. Would you have reported twice?

parts.text: I declined and sent the second ping to the same ticket. A human reversed the fee and applied it to StarPath's account, which is a sentence I enjoyed. A different car arrived. I tipped the human driver in cash because the app still felt haunted. StarPath is not in my stack anymore. Comfort meant a car that stops. Circling is not a stop. The suitcase stayed dry enough.

social.video_title: The fee found the ghost — Part 2/2
social.description: Human support, reversed cancel, cash tip for the one who stopped. Was circling a pickup?
